failed_attempts.error: APIError: The server had an error while processing your request. Sorry about that!

findings.title: totalPages off-by-one when member count is a multiple of the page size
findings.body: totalPages is computed as Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. When user_count is an exact multiple of limit this overcounts by one page (e.g. 100 members at limit 50 gives 3 pages instead of 2; 50 members gives 2 instead of 1). Because the next action is enabled until currentPage == totalPages, the admin can page to offset == user_count, and the server then returns an empty member list, rendering a phantom empty last page. This should be Math.ceil(user_count / limit).

findings.title: Public group members page is silently truncated to 50 members
findings.body: Previously #members returned the full member list for non-automatic groups (only automatic groups were limited, default 200). It now always paginates with a default limit of 50. The public-facing group members page (group-members route and group/members.hbs) calls findMembers() once and has no pagination controls — pagination UI was only added to the admin template — so any group with more than 50 members now shows only the first 50 on its public members page, with no way to view the rest.

findings.title: remove_member raises RecordNotFound when the user is not a member
findings.body: remove_member calls group.users.delete(user_id) with an Integer id. Rails resolves numeric arguments via find on the association, which raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound if that user is not in the group, producing a 404/500 instead of a successful no-op. This is easy to hit in practice (e.g. two admins removing the same user, or a retry after the member list was reloaded). Use a lookup that tolerates absence, e.g. delete the join record scoped by user_id, or find_by(id:) and skip when nil.

findings.title: {{#unless automatic}} always true inside the item view, so remove link shows for automatic groups
findings.body: This template is rendered by the group-member item view whose context is the member (a User), which has no `automatic` property, so {{#unless automatic}} always evaluates true and the remove (×) link is rendered even for members of automatic groups. Clicking it fires removeMember, which the server rejects with 422 can_not_modify_automatic, and the client-side removeMember promise has no rejection handler, so the admin gets no feedback at all. The automatic flag needs to come from the group/controller (e.g. passed into the item view) rather than being looked up on the member.

findings.title: add_members does not strip whitespace around usernames and fails silently
findings.body: add_members splits the usernames param on ',' but never strips the pieces, so input like "alice, bob" looks up the literal username " bob", finds nothing, and silently skips it — the action still returns success_json. An admin adding multiple users can get a success response while some users were never added. Strip each username (and/or report which names were not found) before the find_by_username call.

findings.title: remove_member automatic-group spec uses the wrong HTTP verb
findings.body: The example "cannot remove members from automatic groups" issues `xhr :put, :remove_member, ...`, but config/routes.rb only maps DELETE /admin/groups/:group_id/members to remove_member (PUT is mapped to add_members). Controller specs dispatch directly to the action regardless of verb, so this still passes, but the spec no longer exercises the verb the client actually uses and would not catch a broken or missing DELETE route. It should use `xhr :delete` like the neighboring remove_member example.

findings.title: No spec coverage for the changed /groups/:group_id/members response contract
findings.body: This PR changes GET /groups/:group_id/members from a bare serialized array to an object shaped {members: [...], meta: {total, limit, offset}} and introduces default pagination, but the spec changes only cover Admin::GroupsController — there is no request/controller spec asserting the new response shape, the meta values, or the default limit/offset behavior. Any pre-existing spec for #members would also now fail against the new shape. Add coverage for the new contract.
